title.narrative: Parliamentarians for Global Action Core Support 2019-2021

description.narrative:
Parliamentarians for Global Action (PGA) is a non-governmental, multi-party, international network of legislators mobilizing parliamentarians in all regions of the world to advocate for human rights and rule of law, democracy, human security, inclusion and gender equality. Sida provides core support to PGA's strategic plan 2019-2021, which is aimed at contributing to PGAs vision of a rules-based international order for a more equitable, safe and democratic world through its three programs as below. All programmes and actions of PGA are organized into results-oriented campaigns and PGA works with the following nine campaigns during the period 2019-2021 (the FAW campaign was added in 2020) within each of the three programs: - Core campaign on Democratic Renewal and Human Rights 1) International Law and Human Rights - Campaign of the Universality and Effectiveness of the Rome Statute of the International Criminal Court (ICC) system -Campaign for the Abolition of the Death Penalty (ADP) -Campaign for the Protection of the Oceans and Implementation of SDG 14 2) Gender, Equality and Inclusion -Campaign on Ending Child, Early and Forced Marriage (CEFM) -Campaign against Discrimination based on Sexual Orientation and Gender Identity (SOGI
3) International Peace and Security - Campaign to Address the Illicit Trade in Small Arms and Light Weapons (SALW) and Improved Regulation of the International Arms Trade to Prevent Human Rights Abuses - Campaign for Universality and Implementation of the Biological and Toxin Weapons Convention (BWC) and Implementation of UN Security Council Resolution 1540 (2004) -Campaign in support of the negotiation of a treaty prohibiting fully autonumous weapons (FAW) (added in 2020) - Global Cybersecurity Initiative (added in 2021)

Insatsen avser ett kärnstöd till Parliamentarians for Global Action (PGA) om totalt 9 MNSEK för att implementera sin strategiska plan "Mobilizing Legislators as Champions for Human Rights, Democracy and Peace" under perioden 2019-2021.
Insatsen syftar till att mobilisera parlamentsledamöter att bidra till en internationell ordning baserad på internationella regelverk för en mer rättvis, säker och demokratisk värld. Detta genom arbete mot 8 målområden:
- Universalitet och effektivitet av Romstadgan av den internationella brottmålsdomstolen (ICC) och dess system - Universalitet och implementering av konventionen om biologiska och kemiska vapen (BWC) samt implementering av FN's säkerhetsrådsresolution 1540 (2004) - Förhindra den olagliga handeln med lätta vapen (SALW) samt förbättrad reglering av internationell vapenhandel för att förhindra övergrepp på mänskliga rättigheter - Stoppa barn- och tidiga tvingande äktenskap - Stoppa diskriminering på basis av sexuell orientering och genus identitet - Stoppa dödsstraffen - Skydd av haven och implementering av SDG 14 - Säkerställa att demokratiska normer, institutioner och civilt och politiskt utrymme, inklusive lagstiftares grundläggande rättigheter, är skyddade och uppehållna
PGA's totala organisationsbudget för projektperioden 2019-2021 är 62 MNSEK, av vilken PGA efterfrågar 9 MNSEK (14,5%) från Sida i kärnstöd. Den återstående delen planeras att täckas av medel från Danmark, Kanada, Nederländerna, Estland, Schweiz, Liechtenstein (Global Equality Fund), mellanstatliga organisationer som UNSCAR och EU kommissionen samt stiftelser och fonder så som Stewart R Mott Foundation, Arcus Foundation, CRDF Global, Oak Foundation, Open Society Foundations, Planethood Foundation, Raymond & Elizabeth Bloch Foundation och Sigrid Rausing Trust.

Parliamentarians for Global Action has applied to Sida for core funding of 9 million SEK to implement their strategic plan "Mobilizing Legislators as Champions for Human Rights, Democracy and Peace" during the period 2019-2021.
The intervention aims to moblize legislators to contribute to a rules based international order for a more equitable, safe and democratic world. PGA will work through campaigns focused at 8 overarching objectives:
- Universality and Effectiveness of the Rome Statute of the International Criminal Court (ICC) system - Universality and Implementation of the Biological and Toxin Weapons Convention (BWC) and Implementation of UN Security Council Resolution 1540 (2004) - Addressing the Illicit Trade in Small Arms and Light Weapons (SALW) and Improved Regulation of the International Arms Trade to Prevent Human Rights Abuses - Ending Child, Early and Forced Marriage (CEFM) - Ending Discrimination based on Sexual Orientation and Gender Identity (SOGI) - Abolition of the Death Penalty (ADP) - Protection of the Oceans and Implementation of SDG 14 (to conserve and sustainably use the oceans, seas and marine resources) - Democratic Renewal and Human Rights (in development)
The Global Parliamentary Campaign for Democratic Renewal and Human Rights, is a new Campaign intended to contribute directly to PGA’s vision by supporting the networking mechanism among all parliamentary associations and legislative caucuses.
The interventions total budget for the period 2019-2021 is estimated to 62 million SEK contributed by Institutional donors, Foundations and other Private entities.

Sida has supported PGA since 1996 and with core funding since 2003. PGA works with individual parliamentarians in their national contexts and parliaments, and then leverages that capacity with international networking to support democracy, human rights and peace. This is done through educating, sensitizing, building the technical capacity and strengthening the will of parliamentarians to take ownership, take initiatives and take legislative action. Some of the most important and relevant results during the reporting period, 2019 2021 that have been achieved in PGAs campaigns are: 1) Core Campaign for Democratic Renewal and Human Rights PGA launched in May 2020 the Parliamentary Rapid Response Team (PARRT), which responded to an important number of situations condemning the persecution, incarceration, abuses and serious human rights violations against MPs and Human Rights Defenders and provided policy and legal technical assistance upon request in Argentina, Brazil, Cameroon, Ecuador, Ethiopia, Iran, the Maldives, Myanmar, the Philippines, Russia, Sudan, Ukraine, Venezuela and Zimbabwe. The PARRT cooperated with the European Parliament on its project, Solidarity with Parliamentarians. PGA also prepared and disseminated the Global Parliamentary Code of Democratic Conduct. As of April 2023, the Code of Conduct has been signed by 112 MPs from 50 countries. 2) Campaign to end Child, Early and Forced marriage PGA contributed to legislation in the Dominican Republic (2020), Kenya (2021) and the Philippines (2020)and raised awareness, provided policy and legal technical assistance upon request and contributed to increased political will by engaging MPs in Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Dominican Republic, Ecuador, Kenya, the Maldives, Mozambique, Philippines, Uganda and Zimbabwe. 3) Campaign to end Discrimination Based on Sexual Orientation and Gender Identity /SOGI) During the strategy period PGA contributed to legislation in Barbados, Chile, Dominican Republic, Honduras and Italy and improved parliamentarians understanding of SOGI and encouraged them to take actions that increase social inclusion of LGBTI persons. PGAs LGBTI Inclusion Site received over 55,000 visitors from January 2019 to December 2021. PGA and UNDPs joint SOGI Handbook has been read or downloaded almost 36,000 times in English and Spanish. The Handbook is also available in in Chinese, French, Portuguese, Russian, Thai, Turkish and Vietnamese (an updated and revised Handbook was published in 2022 in English). 4) Campaign for the Abolition of the Death Penalty PGA provided support and technical assistance upon request to MPs working on abolition of the death penalty including to: Central African Republic, Chad, the Gambia, Guinea, Jordan, Lebanon, the Maldives, Mali, Mauritania, Morocco, the Philippines, Sri Lanka, Trinidad and Tobago, and Turkey. PGA also reached out to memberparliamentarians from target countries to advocate for the United Nations General Assembly biannual Resolution calling for a worldwide moratorium on the use of the death penalty, which was adopted in December 2020 with 123 votes in favor, 38 against and 24 abstentions. 5) Campaign for the Effectiveness and Universality of the Rome Statute of the International Criminal Court In Mali, PGA provided its members a full analysis of the criminal framework relating to international criminal justice and of the projet de loi dentente nationale (governments Bill on national unity), which was introduced to Parliament in January 2019. In February 2019, the Legislative Assembly of Costa Rica adopted the Draft Law on Cooperation with the ICC, which was signed into law in May 2019. The legislation was, in large part, the result of the concerted efforts by PGA members. Efforts to undermine the integrity of the Rome Statute system, including addressing misconceptions about the Court and deliberate misinformation driven by political motives has been an important challenge. The biggest threat according to PGA in 2019-2020 was the financial sanctions and travel bans against ICC officials, including the ICC Prosecutor, imposed by the Trump Administration in the United States. PGA closely coordinated with NGOs, high profile figures and other entities to formulate a counter-narrative to dispel misconceptions and combat disinformation regarding the ICC, its mandate and the relationship with US interests. Security challenges, political crises and the erosion of human rights limited progress in Cameroon, Iraq, Togo, Ukraine and Zimbabwe (despite a successful visit of Zimbabwean PGA members to the ICC in March 2020). 6) Campaign for the Protection of the Oceans and Implementation of SDG 14 PGA has facilitated the signature of the International Maritime Organizations (IMO) Torremolinos Declaration in 14 countries, including: Argentina, Belize, Central African Republic, Chile, Congo (Republic of), Costa Rica, Democratic Republic of Congo, Gabon, Guinea (Republic of), Guinea Bissau, Mozambique, Namibia, Nigeria and São Tomé and Príncipe. PGA also contributed to action in the Maldives, which deposited intent to ratify in 2021. 7) Campaign to Address the Threat of Weapons of Mass Destruction In Chile the Chamber of Deputies approved a Bill presented by a PGA MP to implement the Biological Weapons Convention and Chemical Weapons Convention into domestic Law and passed domestic implementing legislation in July 2020. The Solomon Islands submitted its First National Report to UNSCR 1540 Committee in December 2019 as a result of the leading role played by PGA members in this process and Tanzania ratified the BWC in August 2019 also as a result of the leading role played by PGA members in this process. 8) Campaign to Address the Illicit Trade in Small Arms and Light Weapons and Promote Ratification and Implementation of the Arms Trade Treaty (ATT) With PGA technical support to MP members of PGA the ATT was ratified by Botswana, Namibia and São Tomé and Príncipe. Membership: PGA noted several positive trends in 20192021: The percentage of female member parliamentarians grew from 33% to 36% and, while membership has decreased overall, membership increased in Africa and the Middle East. PGA Membership in Afghanistan As a sign of solidarity and support for PGAs elected Members of the Afghanistan Parliament, PGAs Board extended membership of Afghan elected Lawmakers ousted from their constitutionally mandated role by the Talibans unconstitutional takeover of the territory of Afghanistan in 2021 and self-proclamation of the Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan. This is the second time that PGAs Board extended membership to parliamentarians removed from office by violent means after the 2013 Coup détat in the Central African Republic. Afghanistans Parliamentarians will remain PGA Members as if they were Parliamentarians until the time in which their constitutional mandate would have expired in 2023. Bedömning av uppnådda resultat i förhållande till insatsens mål The support provided to PGA has achieved good results over the three year period in relation to the objectives of the intervention. These results include the following: In relation to the objectives for the parliamentary campaign for the effectiveness and universality of the Rome Statute (RS) of the ICC system through PGA's efforts throughout the threeyear period there has been strenghtened political will in support of the fight against impunity. There has been one new ratification (Kiribati) of the RS during the activity period but there has also been significant progress toward ratification in many countries. In addition there has also been significant achievements toward effective domestic implementation of the RS within states and PGA has actively contributed to the process of drafting and amending national legislation aimed at implementting the RS into domestic legal systems. PGA has directly contributed to 75 of the 118 state ratifications/ accessions to the RS that remain legally valid to date as well as the adoption of legislative packages on domestic implemenation in 37 states. In relation to the objectives for the global platform for the abolition of the death penalty through PGA's efforts there has been strengthened political will and awareness on the importance of abolising the death penalty. These have led to modification of national legal systems for the abolition of the death penalty or blocking of its reinstatement or resumption of executions. Strong advocacy was also performed by PGA, through the World Coalition Against the Death Penalty, so that an UNGA resolution on a new moratorium on the use of the death penalty was adopted. In relation to the objectives for the campaign to end child, early and forces marriages (CEFM) some progress has been made towards countries amending their legislation to protect the rights of girls and women through a strengthened political will and awareness to reform discriminatory provisions and to end child, early and forced marriage. PGA support has also raised awareness among MPs on their role to implement the 2030 Agenda and through the dissemination of the toolkit The role of parliamentarians to end child marriages prepared by Girls Not Brides. PGA has however also struggled to maintain its members' level of engagement within this campaing, partly due to competing political interests but also due to a lack of dedicated funding. In relation to the objectives for the campaign against discrimination based on sexual orientation and gender identity (SOGI) PGA has supported an improved understanding and political will among MPs for legislative reform about nondiscrimination based on SOGI during the activity period. PGAs SOGI campaign has during the activity period grown to become a trusted partner to LGBTI activists, NGOs, UN agencies and National Human Rights Institutions. Interactions between MPs and LGBTQI activists were strenghtened and PGA members contributed to legislative reform. In addition advocacy and communication was strengthened through the publishing and wide dissemination of a handbook for parliamentarians on LGBTQI in a joint PGA/UNDP project. In 2020, the COVID19 pandemic shifted priorities all over the world. PGA postponed all planned inperson activities and readjusted to a new reality of virtual events but this is particularly challenging for the SOGI Campaign, since the work greatly benefits from bringing MPs and LGBTI activists together in person which increases the opportunities to build empathy and bridges of communication resulting in better outcomes. In relation to the objectives for the campaign for the universality and implementation of the Arms Trade Treaty (ATT) and the Biological and Toxin Weapons Convention (BTWC) PGA members have taken extensive initiatives to promote ratification and implementation of the BTWC during the activity period which has lead to accessions or concrete steps taken towards the ratification to the. PGA has also provided important input and advocacy outreach leading to new draft legislation in countries. In relation to the ATT PGA members have made important, measurable contributions to moving the ATT signature process forward in 44 of the 141 UN member states that signed ATT as well as visavis 45 of the 113 UN member states that have currently ratified the ATT to date. In addition PGA has secured commitments from a range of MPs to take action so that their countries submit national reports to the UN program of action on Small Arms and Light Weapons (SALW) on a more regular basis.
During the period PGA has updated the strategic plan in accordance with changing context including through adding planned outputs in the yearly plan as relevant or for example also worked on advocacy to stop potential withdrawal from the RS/ICC or also included work on legislative initiatives aimed at blocking of its reinstatement or resumption of execution. PGA has also launched and developed new campaigns, ie the Campaign for protection of the oceans as well as the Campaign for democratic renewal and human rights which both has started in 2019 within the new Sida core support to PGA. PGA has also, towards the end of the activity period, worked to strengthen its RBM approach, with support from Sida, including linking programme objectives to strategic objectives and making the theory of change more explicit, including the identification of key assumptions and risks. This has led to that PGA should now be better at developing a clearer change story, giving stakeholders a more precise understanding of PGA's work and methodology. As to the sustainability of results PGA work depends very much on the motivations and capacities of MPs to advocate for and take possible steps towards change in legislation towards ratifications. As ratification processes are long processes the sustainability of planned results (ratification) also can be jepardized by elections in countries, which potentially may led to new MPs taking power, with different agendas than the previous ones working with PGA. However PGA is aware of this challenge and is working with recommendations from civil society and sitting MPs to see which new MPs could be drafted to PGA in case of a major shift in the parliament after an election. PGA is also a rather small organisation which relies on funding from only a few coresupport donors and a larger number of donors which provide earmarked support particular campaigns, which makes PGA, or rather certain campaigns, more vulnerable to trends in the donor community. PGA has in recent years operationalized a PGA Development Advisory Committee, which among others are supposed toprovide strategic input, increase visibility and augment fundraising. Sida assesses that this demonstrates an increased ambition for a more strategic resource mobilization. The strengthened RBM approach that PGA has embarked upon should also lead to a strenghtened strategic direction and positive effects on resource mobilization. In addition Sida will, in the new support 20222024, encourage and partake in donor coordination to support a development which will enable PGA to uphold its strategic direction and resource the planned work under all of its main objectives.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
